html:
The Kayambi are a Kichwa speaking people of the northern highlands of Ecuador, around the Cayambe volcano northeast of Quito.

In the late 1400s the Kayambi and their allies, including the Caranqui and the peoples around Otavalo, held out for years against the Inca armies of Huayna Capac. Tradition says the Inca killed so many at the end that the lake where it happened was named Yahuarcocha, "lake of blood". Under Spanish rule they worked on large haciendas. In the 1900s Kayambi leaders such as Dolores Cacuango organized the first Indigenous unions of Ecuador, and today the Kayambi are part of the wider Kichwa movement.
sum: The Kayambi are a Kichwa speaking people of the northern highlands of Ecuador, around the Cayambe volcano northeast of Quito.
